column4: configuration only
column6: Standard Linux device selection belongs beside the drivers it controls.

column4: build composition only
column6: Kbuild ownership cannot be supplied by an outer host provider.

column6: The kernel-side channel adapter preserves the standard UML console and channel ABI.

column4: outer host owns Darwin file services
column6: The declaration is consumed by the in-kernel channel implementation.

column4: outer host owns backing-file syscalls
column6: Copy-on-write block semantics and metadata validation remain a Linux device concern.

column4: outer host owns SLiRP packets and readiness
column6: The kernel endpoint is a small standard net_device adapter; SLiRP state and policy are already outside Linux.

column4: outer host owns management-console requests
column6: The declarations bind kernel-owned management commands to the UML console dispatcher.

column4: outer host owns management-console requests
column6: Linux PM ordering, CPU hotplug, device suspension, and wake-source semantics must remain inside the guest kernel.

column4: outer host owns management-console requests
column6: The command table selects kernel interrupt or process context and therefore remains part of the UML kernel console.

column4: outer host owns clock primitives
column6: Linux RTC registration and interrupt semantics must remain in the guest kernel.

column4: outer host owns Darwin timing calls
column6: This is the UML host-boundary half of the standard RTC driver, not a replaceable application service.

column4: outer host owns channel file descriptors
column6: Linux serial-line registration and its configured port ceiling remain standard UML device policy.

column4: outer host owns file descriptors and mappings
column6: Linux block queues and UBD request semantics remain in the kernel.

column4: outer host owns Darwin file and mapping primitives
column6: The UML user half translates standard UBD requests at the established OS boundary.

column4: outer host owns vhost-user GPU service
column6: Virtio discovery, queues, and IRQ delivery remain kernel responsibilities; the generic 64-bit DMA-mask correction is isolated as topic 0014 so a later base audit can drop it independently from Darwin topic 0010.

column4: outer host owns VNC server and input transport
column6: The outer provider emits events; Linux input-device registration and event injection stay in the kernel.

column4: outer wrapper cannot replace Kbuild internals
column6: The modules.builtin.modinfo rule must trim trailing NUL padding with a host-portable in-place command.

column4: outer wrapper may invoke but cannot safely rewrite link policy
column6: The script owns linker capability selection for the final image.

column4: outer wrapper cannot alter compiled host-tool types
column6: Darwin's system uuid_t collides with the Linux device-table type before an outer wrapper can intervene.
